title: Qatar and France Sign Bilateral Letter of Intent on Digital Cooperation Highlighting Shared Quantum Ambitions - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
The State of Qatar and the French Republic have signed a bilateral Letter of Intent (LoI) to strengthen cooperation across artificial intelligence, digital transformation, and emerging technologies, explicitly highlighting quantum technologies as a shared strategic priority. Formalized in Doha on the sidelines of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26), the agreement was signed by Qatar’s Minister of Communications and Information Technology, H.E. Mohammed bin Ali Al Mannai, and France’s Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs, H.E. Anne Le Hénanff.

According to Qatar’s Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), the framework establishes mechanisms for exchanging technical expertise, developing digital applications across priority economic sectors, and building local digital competencies. During the signing, Minister Le Hénanff noted that both governments share a common vision of strategic autonomy in the digital sector and aligned ambitions in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies.

While the ministerial LoI is a broad information and communications technology framework without disclosed project funding or binding procurement targets, it reinforces growing commercial ties between the two countries. Two days prior to the ministerial signing, French photonic quantum computing developer Quandela finalized a tripartite deployment alliance in Doha with Qatari technology group Mekdam Holding Group and sovereign data center operator MEEZA to bring cloud and on-premises quantum systems to the Gulf region.
